description: The >>DEFINE compilation-variable-name AS { literal | arithmetic-expression | PARAMETER | OFF } [OVERRIDE] compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.11) - it defines the compilation variables the §2023:7.3.16 IF and §2023:7.3.13 EVALUATE directives and §2023:13.10 constant entries read. Implemented by ConditionalCompilationProcessor; the introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2002. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 has no compiler directives, its only compiler-directing forms being statements (§1985:IV.6.4.2.2.1: 'The compiler directing verbs are COPY, ENTER, REPLACE, and USE'), so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduces the directive (§2002:7.2.2 SR5: 'A compiler directive is composed of the compiler directive indicator') and §2002:F.2 lists the facility as a change, its item 29: 'Compiler directives instruct the compiler to take specific actions during compilation'. The directive is in the 2002 text: §2002:7.2.9: 'The DEFINE directive specifies a symbolic name, called a compilation variable'; §2002:7.2.4: 'The compiler directives that are used for conditional compilation are the DEFINE directive, the EVALUATE directive, and the IF directive'; and §2002:F.2 names it, its item 32: 'Directives are provided to enable specific lines of source to be included or omitted'. 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.3.9: 'The DEFINE directive specifies a symbolic name, called a compilation variable') and so does 2023 (§2023:7.3.11.1).

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.11.2 general format + §2023:7.3.11.3: a compilation-variable-name with AS / OFF / PARAMETER / OVERRIDE and a compile-time expression — diagnosed by the conditional-compilation driver as COBOL1618/COBOL1619.

source:
>>DEFINE XX AS 1
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725DF.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
